cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: The method should reject a null Message and throw NPE, regardless of error code or old TSIG.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: A negative error code is invalid; the method should throw an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: Message contains a new TSIGRecord with RCODE=0 (NOERROR)
cases.description: When error == 0 and no previous TSIG, a normal TSIG should be generated and attached to the message.

cases.expected: Message contains a new TSIGRecord whose RCODE matches the supplied error (9 = NOTIMP)
cases.description: When a non‑zero error code is supplied, the generated TSIG must carry that error in its RCODE field.

cases.expected: Generated TSIGRecord has a zero time‑signed field (no prior record to copy).
cases.description: When old == null the algorithm should treat this as the first TSIG in the transaction.

cases.expected: Generated TSIGRecord copies the timeSigned from the old record (or increments it according to spec).
cases.description: When an old TSIG is supplied, the new TSIG must incorporate the previous time‑signed value to allow proper verification.

cases.expected: Same result as calling apply(m, error, old, true)
cases.description: The three‑argument overload should delegate to the four‑argument version with fullSignature set to true.

cases.expected: TSIGException propagated
cases.description: If the underlying four‑argument method throws, the three‑argument wrapper must not swallow the exception.

input.value: mock(Message) with no TSIG, current time = Instant.now()
TSIGRecord with timeSigned = Instant.now().minus(TSIG.FUDGE).plusSeconds(1) (just inside the fudge window)

cases.expected: Message receives a TSIGRecord whose timeSigned is within the allowed FUDGE duration; no exception is thrown.
cases.description: When the previous TSIG’s timeSigned is just inside the allowed fudge window, apply should accept it and generate a new TSIG without raising a BADTIME error.

input.value: mock(Message) with no TSIG, current time = Instant.now()
TSIGRecord with timeSigned = Instant.now().minus(TSIG.FUDGE).minusSeconds(1) (just outside the fudge window)

cases.expected: TSIGException (or IllegalArgumentException) indicating BADTIME because the old timeSigned is outside the allowed fudge period.
cases.description: When the previous TSIG’s timeSigned is just outside the allowed fudge window, apply must reject it and surface a BADTIME‑related error.

group: Algorithm mismatch between old TSIG and new

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: If the algorithm of the supplied old TSIG differs from the algorithm configured in the TSIG instance (default HMAC_MD5), the method should reject the call with an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: TSIGException (or IllegalArgumentException) because the TSIG instance was constructed with an empty secret key.
cases.description: A TSIG object whose secret key byte array is zero‑length cannot compute a MAC; apply must fail with a clear exception.

input.value: mock(Message) that already contains a TSIGRecord

cases.expected: IllegalStateException (or TSIGException) indicating that a TSIG is already present on the message.
cases.description: Calling apply on a Message that already carries a TSIG should not silently replace it; the method is expected to reject the operation.

input.note: 18 is the DNS RCODE for BADTIME

cases.expected: Message contains a TSIGRecord whose RCODE field equals 18 (BADTIME) and whose timeSigned is set to the current Instant.
cases.description: When the caller supplies the BADTIME error code, apply must embed that code in the generated TSIG while also setting a fresh timeSigned value.

input.value: mock(Message) with a few question and answer records

cases.expected: Generated TSIGRecord MAC length matches the expected output size of the default algorithm (16 bytes for HMAC‑MD5).
cases.description: The three‑argument overload forwards to the four‑argument version with fullSignature=true; consequently the full message (including all sections) is covered by the MAC. The test verifies the MAC size matches the algorithm’s output length.

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: The TSIG instance was constructed with a null secret key. Calling apply should detect the missing secret and throw NPE before any MAC computation.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: The TSIG object was created with an algorithm name that is not recognised (e.g., "HMAC-FOO"). apply should fail during MAC initialisation and raise an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: TSIGException (BADTIME)
cases.description: When the old TSIG’s timeSigned is in the future beyond the allowed fudge period, apply must reject the request and surface a BADTIME‑related TSIGException.

input.value: TSIGRecord using HMAC_SHA256 but with a truncated MAC (e.g., 10 bytes instead of 32)

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: The old TSIG record contains a MAC whose length does not match the output size of the configured algorithm. apply should validate the MAC length and throw IllegalArgumentException.

group: Error code out of valid range

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: DNS RCODE values are limited to 0‑65535. Supplying a value larger than this should cause apply to reject the argument with IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalStateException
cases.description: A DNS message may contain at most one TSIG. If the message already holds two TSIG records, apply should detect the inconsistency and throw IllegalStateException.

input.value: TSIGRecord whose key name differs from the TSIG instance’s key name

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: If the supplied old TSIG uses a different key name than the TSIG object’s configured name, the method must reject the call with IllegalArgumentException.
